questions.q: A 28-year-old male presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis for 10 days with firm, non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy shows motile spirochetes. Which is the treatment of choice?
opts: Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM single dose
questions.exp: Primary syphilis (chancre) is treated with Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM as a single dose — the drug of choice per CDC/WHO. Doxycycline is the alternative for penicillin-allergic patients.

questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a verrucous plaque on the dorsum of the foot with black dots on the surface. KOH mount shows 'copper penny' cells (muriform/sclerotic bodies). What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis presents with verrucous plaques and the hallmark of 'copper penny' cells (Medlar bodies) on KOH or histology — brown, thick-walled, septate cells. Mycetoma shows grains in pus, not sclerotic bodies.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with tense bullae on normal and erythematous skin, predominantly in the flexures. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 at the dermo-epidermal junction. Which antigen is targeted?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid targets BP180 (BPAG2/type XVII collagen) and BP230. Linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF is characteristic. Desmoglein 1 and 3 are targets in pemphigus; type VII collagen in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

questions.q: A 22-year-old student presents with grouped vesicles over the right T5 dermatome with burning pain preceding the rash by 2 days. He is immunocompetent. What is the first-line antiviral and ideal time window?
questions.exp: Herpes zoster is treated with Valacyclovir 1 g TDS for 7 days, started within 72 hours of rash onset to reduce severity and postherpetic neuralgia risk. Famciclovir 500 mg TDS is equally effective. IV acyclovir is for immunocompromised or disseminated disease.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male from Bihar presents with a hypopigmented anaesthetic patch on his cheek. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocyte cuffing and no AFB. What type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with a single well-defined anaesthetic hypopigmented patch. Histology shows well-formed epithelioid granulomas with lymphocytes and nerve involvement within the granuloma. Smear is negative (paucibacillary). BT has multiple lesions with less well-formed granulomas.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman has progressive skin tightening over the hands and face, Raynaud's phenomenon, and dysphagia. ANA is positive with anticentromere antibody pattern. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody is characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc/CREST: Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia). Diffuse SSc is associated with anti-Scl-70 (anti-topoisomerase I).

questions.q: A 55-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders, telangiectasias, and central ulceration on the nose after long-term sun exposure. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Nodular BCC classically presents as a pearly papule with rolled pearlescent borders, surface telangiectasias, and central ulceration on sun-exposed skin. The nose is the most common site; BCC is the most common skin cancer.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female has butterfly-shaped malar erythema sparing the nasolabial folds with photosensitivity. ANA 1:640 (speckled), anti-dsDNA elevated. Which mechanism best explains the photosensitivity in SLE?
opts: UVB induces keratinocyte apoptosis exposing nuclear antigens
UV radiation upregulates IL-4 causing B-cell activation
questions.exp: In SLE, UVB induces keratinocyte apoptosis, exposing nuclear antigens (Ro/SSA, La/SSB) on cell surfaces. These are recognized by autoantibodies, triggering immune complex deposition and inflammation — the basis of photosensitivity and the malar rash.

questions.q: A 19-year-old male has multiple soft, flesh-colored pedunculated papules in the axillae and groin. His father has similar lesions and café-au-lait macules. What is the inheritance pattern of this condition?
questions.exp: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) presents with café-au-lait macules, neurofibromas, axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe's sign), and Lisch nodules. It follows autosomal dominant inheritance with a mutation in the NF1 gene on chromosome 17.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman on long-term hydroxychloroquine for lupus develops blue-grey pigmentation over sun-exposed areas and the hard palate. What is the mechanism of this pigmentation?
opts: Drug-melanin complex deposition in the dermis
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine and other antimalarials cause pigmentation through drug-melanin complex formation deposited in the dermis, producing blue-grey discoloration in sun-exposed areas, shins, and hard palate.

questions.q: A 32-year-old HIV-positive male (CD4 80 cells/μL) has painful purple-red plaques on the lower limbs and oral mucosa. Biopsy shows spindle cell proliferation with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated RBCs. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in AIDS is caused by HHV-8 (KSHV). Histology shows spindle cells, slit-like vascular spaces, and extravasated RBCs. It typically occurs at CD4 count <200 cells/μL.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male has a non-healing ulcer on the lower leg for 3 months with irregular sloping edges, a necrotic base, and surrounding induration. Biopsy shows invasive dysplastic squamous epithelium. Which pre-existing condition most increases SCC risk here?
questions.exp: SCC arising in a chronic wound or scar is called Marjolin's ulcer. Chronic venous ulcers, burn scars, and osteomyelitis sinuses can undergo malignant transformation. SCC in this setting is aggressive with higher metastatic potential.

questions.q: A 28-year-old female has erythema, scaling, and pustules at the scalp margin with permanent central scarring alopecia. Wood's lamp shows bright green fluorescence of the affected hairs. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Favus is caused by Trichophyton schoenleinii and shows bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. It produces scutula (yellowish crusts) around hair follicles and leads to permanent scarring alopecia. Kerion (M. canis or T. tonsurans) fluoresces blue-green.

questions.q: A patient with lepromatous leprosy on MDT suddenly develops erythema and edema of existing lesions, fever, and joint pains over 2 days, with no new lesions or nerve tenderness. What is the reaction and its first-line treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL/Type 2 reaction) occurs in LL and BL leprosy: tender erythematous nodules/plaques, fever, and systemic symptoms. First-line is thalidomide (males) or prednisolone. Clofazimine is used for recurrent/chronic ENL.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male has multiple firm skin-colored papules along the lower eyelids. Histology shows cystic and solid nests of basaloid cells with comma-shaped ductal lumina in a fibrous stroma. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Syringomas are benign eccrine sweat duct tumors presenting as small skin-colored papules typically on the lower eyelids. Histology shows tadpole/comma-shaped ductal structures derived from eccrine ducts.

questions.q: A 16-year-old obese male on recent broad-spectrum antibiotics develops pruritic erythema and scaling in the intertriginous areas. KOH shows hyphae and budding yeast. Which systemic antifungal is now contraindicated due to severe hepatotoxicity?
questions.exp: Systemic ketoconazole is no longer recommended due to severe hepatotoxicity and adrenal suppression. FDA and EMA have restricted its systemic use. Fluconazole and itraconazole are safe alternatives. Terbinafine has limited anti-Candida activity.

questions.q: A 38-year-old woman has heliotrope rash around the eyes, Gottron's papules over MCP/PIP joints, and proximal muscle weakness with markedly elevated CK. Which antibody carries the highest risk of interstitial lung disease?
questions.exp: Anti-Jo-1 is the most common anti-synthetase antibody in dermatomyositis/polymyositis and is strongly associated with ILD, mechanic's hands, Raynaud's, and arthritis (anti-synthetase syndrome). Anti-Mi-2 carries a good prognosis; anti-TIF-1γ is associated with cancer-associated myositis.

questions.q: A 24-year-old female has recurrent oral ulcers (>3/year), genital ulcers, and uveitis. Pathergy test is positive. Which HLA type is most strongly associated with this condition?
questions.exp: Behçet's disease (recurrent oral/genital ulcers, uveitis, pathergy positivity) is strongly associated with HLA-B51, especially in Middle Eastern and Asian populations.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child has multiple yellowish-orange papules and nodules on the scalp and face. Histology shows large foam cells and Touton giant cells. Serum lipids are normal. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Juvenile xanthogranuloma (JXG) is the most common non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis in children: yellow-orange papules on head/neck, Touton giant cells (peripheral foamy cytoplasm with a wreath of nuclei) on histology. Serum lipids normal; lesions often regress spontaneously.

questions.q: A 42-year-old male on dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops acute hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia. Which enzyme deficiency most predisposes to dapsone-induced hemolysis?
questions.exp: G6PD deficiency is the most important predisposing factor for dapsone-induced hemolytic anemia. G6PD is required for the HMP shunt to generate NADPH, protecting RBCs from oxidative stress. Dapsone's hydroxylamine metabolites cause oxidative hemolysis, especially in G6PD-deficient patients.

questions.q: A 33-year-old female presents with painful clustered vesicles on the labia majora and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. PCR confirms primary HSV-2 infection. What is the recommended treatment?
questions.exp: Primary genital herpes is treated with Acyclovir 400 mg TDS for 7-10 days (or 200 mg 5×/day for 7-10 days). Valacyclovir 1 g BD or Famciclovir 250 mg TDS for 7-10 days are alternatives. Shorter regimens are for recurrent episodes only.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male with chronic plaque psoriasis is on methotrexate. At what traditional cumulative dose threshold is liver biopsy recommended?
questions.exp: The traditional threshold for liver biopsy in psoriasis patients on methotrexate is 1.5 g cumulative dose. Current guidelines prefer non-invasive monitoring via FibroScan or serum Pro-collagen III N-terminal peptide (PIIINP).

questions.q: A 65-year-old male has a rapidly growing dome-shaped nodule with a central keratin-filled crater on the cheek, present for 6 weeks. Histology shows well-differentiated squamous cells with a central keratin plug and symmetric shoulder architecture. Best management?
opts: Observation; spontaneous regression expected in 3-6 months
questions.exp: Keratoacanthoma (KA) is now often classified as a well-differentiated SCC variant. Despite a tendency to regress, surgical excision with histological confirmation is recommended because clinical and histological distinction from SCC is unreliable and KA can behave aggressively.

questions.q: A 29-year-old sexually active male has matted tender inguinal lymphadenopathy with violaceous overlying skin and a groove sign (between two groups of nodes divided by Poupart's ligament). What is the etiological agent?
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) is caused by Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3. Greenblatt's groove sign (groove between inguinal and femoral nodes divided by Poupart's ligament) is pathognomonic. Treatment: doxycycline 100 mg BD for 21 days.

questions.q: A 55-year-old male farmer presents with sinuses discharging white sulfur granules from a foot swelling, with X-ray evidence of bone destruction. What is the most common cause of eumycetoma in India?
questions.exp: Eumycetoma in India is most commonly caused by Madurella mycetomatis (dark/black grains). Actinomadura madurae (actinomycetoma) produces white grains. Treatment: eumycetoma requires itraconazole ± surgery; actinomycetoma responds to dapsone/co-trimoxazole + streptomycin.

questions.q: A 20-year-old female presents with an itchy ring-shaped scaly plaque on the thigh. KOH mount shows branching septate hyphae. Which dermatophyte is the most common cause of tinea corporis in India?
questions.exp: Trichophyton rubrum is the most common dermatophyte causing tinea corporis globally and in India. Notably, T. indotineae (previously misidentified as T. mentagrophytes) has emerged as a major cause of recalcitrant terbinafine-resistant dermatophytosis in India.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male on biologics for psoriasis develops a demyelinating neurological syndrome. Which class of biologic is contraindicated in patients with MS or demyelinating disease?
questions.exp: TNF-α inhibitors (etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab) are contraindicated in demyelinating diseases because they can worsen or precipitate demyelination. Anti-IL-17, anti-IL-23 agents, and ustekinumab do not carry this contraindication.

questions.q: A newborn presents with large bullae at birth that rupture easily, leaving denuded areas. Nikolsky's sign is positive. Biopsy shows suprabasal cleavage with acantholysis. The mother has active pemphigus vulgaris. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Neonatal pemphigus results from transplacental transfer of maternal IgG anti-desmoglein antibodies (anti-Dsg1/3). Histology shows suprabasal acantholysis. It is transient, resolving as maternal antibodies clear. SSSS shows subcorneal cleavage; EBS has a dermal-epidermal split at the basal layer.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male undergoes Mohs micrographic surgery for a BCC on the nose. What is the key principle distinguishing Mohs surgery from standard excision?
opts: 100% peripheral and deep margin examination with real-time tumor mapping
Wider excision margins than standard surgery
Use of laser technology to ablate residual tumor cells
Frozen section analysis of random tissue samples
questions.exp: Mohs surgery examines 100% of peripheral and deep tissue margins using horizontal frozen sections (vs. standard vertical bread-loaf sections sampling <1% of margins), enabling real-time complete margin assessment and cure rates >99% for primary BCC.

questions.q: A 25-year-old female develops diffuse hair thinning 3 months after delivery. Hemoglobin and TFTs are normal. Hair pull test shows predominantly telogen hairs. What is the most appropriate management?
opts: Reassurance and observation; spontaneous recovery expected
questions.exp: Postpartum telogen effluvium is a physiological shift of hairs from anagen to telogen 2-3 months after delivery (estrogen withdrawal). It is self-limiting, resolving spontaneously within 6-12 months. Reassurance is the primary management. Finasteride is contraindicated in women of childbearing potential.

questions.q: A 48-year-old male has a solitary tender violaceous nodule on the sole that bleeds easily on minor trauma. Dermoscopy shows reddish-black lacunae. Biopsy reveals interconnecting vascular channels lined by endothelial cells without atypia and hemosiderin deposition. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma (hobnail hemangioma) presents as a solitary violaceous nodule with an ecchymotic ring. Dermoscopy shows reddish-black lacunae. Histology reveals dilated vascular channels with hobnail endothelial cells and hemosiderin — benign, no atypia.
